disclaimer: Every published correction is listed here, with the date, what it said and what it says now. The full history is in the repository.
correcoes[0].antes: The Impostômetro annual series carried, for 2019 and 2021, the R$ 2.5 trillion mark hit on 20 December, not the year's total.
correcoes[0].depois: Totals read from the Arrecadação Brasil panel from 1 January to 31 December of each year: 2018 R$ 2,388 bn, 2021 R$ 2,592 bn and 2022 R$ 2,890 bn, among smaller adjustments.
correcoes[1].antes: The infant mortality series mixed two IBGE products: the Life Table and the 2018 Population Projection.
correcoes[1].depois: The whole series now comes from the 2024 Complete Life Table: 28.1 in 2000 and 15.0 in 2010.
correcoes[2].antes: The share of households connected to the sewage network by state was attributed to the Census.
correcoes[2].depois: The values were right; the source is the PNAD Contínua survey, and the page now says so.
correcoes[3].antes: The 82% of municipalities that cannot sustain themselves on their own revenue appeared without a year.
correcoes[3].depois: The figure is from the 2016 National Public Sector Balance; the neighbouring figure, from Poder360, is from 2020. Both now say when they are from.
correcoes[4].antes: It said opening a company took 30 to 45 days until the operating licence.
correcoes[4].depois: The cited report says 7 to 34 hours to formalise, varying 386% between states. What the source supports went in.
correcoes[5].antes: A sentence attributed to President Lula about a single tax rate appeared in quotation marks, as if verbatim.
correcoes[5].depois: The report summarises a post; the sentence was marked as paraphrase and the promise now says "up to 20%", which is what the coverage states.
correcoes[6].antes: The illiteracy pair crossed the 2003 PNAD with the 2024 PNAD Contínua, and the 11.6% for 2003 was not in the cited report.
correcoes[6].depois: The Census pair went in, on the same yardstick: 13.6% in 2000 and 7.0% in 2022.
correcoes[7].antes: Eight promises and one justification appeared in quotation marks although they were an outlet's summary, a translation or a third party's account.
correcoes[7].depois: Each now appears without quotation marks and with the mark "paraphrase, not verbatim". The item on the JBS case, with no inquiry number and outside the site's subject, was removed.
correcoes[8].antes: It attributed to Graça Foster, in quotation marks, that announcing the initial figure for Abreu e Lima "was a mistake".
correcoes[8].depois: The sentence was the Chamber news agency's headline, not her words. The text now reports the testimony and quotes the page's only verbatim sentence.
correcoes[9].antes: The answer about a phone bought abroad was cited as item 1.8 of the Traveller's Guide.
correcoes[9].depois: It is item 1.13; item 1.8 covers vehicle parts.
